text.p: Trailer axle-maker Wassall Asia Pacific Ltd said on Wednesday it expected lower profits due to subdued regional demand and reduced prospects in key markets.

"Due to the continuing subdued demand across the region and reduced prospects for Thailand and other key markets, together with increased pressure on selling prices, it is now likely profit will fall below that reported last year," the company said in a statemen.
In March, the company said in a statement accompanying the release of its financial results for year ended December 31, 1996, that it expected satisfactory results in 1997.
On Wednesday, Wassal said it was taking action to remedy the situation and continued to develop new markets.
In the 1996 financial year, Wassall's net profit grew to Singapore $0.73 million from S$0.10 million.
